items.title: Andrew Morgan Interview, 1961-07-04
items.q: I played with Kit Howard's band after he had a band.

ctx.x: The one who made the records on Columbia. Yeah.

Well, a long while after that, then, um, he was a fella, I don't know, they couldn't get along with him. And then there, this boy, Roy Evans, he came to the band. He played with Sam. And I think he played with Sam until Sam had given up playing music. He died. Sam died. And after that, this boy, he died too. So from that on, I played around the city of New Orleans with different fellows. I played with Kit Howard's band after he had a band. And I played with, uh, George Williams' band. The drummer.

items.title: Avery "Kid" Howard Interview, 1961-05-22
items.q: And then Andrew Morgan came in and they liked what I was doing and they hired me

ctx.x: On drums? No. Well that was something that went about that I said I couldn't play, which I couldn't. I did many times go to parties. And so finally one night, Young Morgan's band, he had his on band at that particular time, and I went to a party and the drummer got hooked. And so when I walked in, they said, well here come a drummer. Well I couldn't get up and I went up and played with him. Jim Robinson was with Young Morgan at that particular time. And then Andrew Morgan came in and they liked what I was doing…

items.title: Avery "Kid" Howard Interview, 1958-12-22
items.q: I play, when I was waking at the farm with Morgan, under Morgan, Andrew Morgan, I used to bring the trumpet and the bass

ctx.x: They both made slide, I guess, all the time. Do you remember any of these vowel trombones when you were a kid? Did somebody play vowels?

Well, I never known a guy that played, but I have seen it because I have played on a vowel trombone, because it's the same thing like the trumpet, you see? And it's like the E flat bass tuba. I play, when I was waking at the farm with Morgan, under Morgan, Andrew Morgan, I used to bring the trumpet and the bass, the straight up bass tuba in place. I play, because it's the same thing. And all the difference is the mouthpiece. I mean, another way you pronounce the notes different, but things the same thing. When I…
I don't think the birds were too loud for that, but we can hear better enough. See, we were talking about the band of the bass and the other bands.
